absent: PIT count load, gate and output evaluation, timer callback, worker dispatch, reinject accounting, and acknowledge handling internals.
Control word decoding for mode and BCD and read write selection beyond the visible count write sequencer.
Speaker dummy flag values and full PIO bus address map outside timer and speaker ranges.
PIC port read path, edge level control programming, poll behavior, and full vCPU delivery beyond wakeup kick.
IO bus lookup, unregister, and eventfd interaction beyond sorted registration.
Userspace structure layouts for legacy and extended PIT state and reinject control.

findings.text: Creation routine allocates a PIT object, initializes its mutex and timer and worker and acknowledgement state, resets channels, enables reinject, and registers timer ports plus optional speaker port, unwinding registrations and worker on failure.
Teardown routine unregisters timer and speaker devices, disables reinject, cancels the timer, destroys the worker and frees the object, doing nothing when no PIT is attached.

Userspace state interface provides legacy channel get and set, extended channel plus flags get and set, and reinject control, all serializing against the PIT mutex and reloading channel counts after a set.
Bus registration inserts a device address range into a sorted table using copy on write replacement with deferred reclamation of the old table.
PIC interface exposes pin level injection for a routed entry, explicit output refresh, interrupt acknowledge returning a vector, and mask notifier broadcast keyed by chip pin mapping.
Timer port accesses first validate range and reduce address by channel mask, with index three treated as control on the write path and as an immediate success path producing no data on the read path.
Count writes honor per channel write sequencing selecting low only, high only, or two part word order with an intermediate latch and state advance between parts.
Timer reads prefer stored status over stored count over live counter, with latched single byte modes consumed in one access and latched word mode consumed across staged accesses.
Live counter reads honor per channel read sequencing, with single byte modes stable across accesses and word mode alternating between low and high parts on successive reads.

Speaker writes update a stored data flag from the second value bit and drive gate for channel two from the low value bit, while reads combine stored data and gate and output with a time derived refresh toggle.
Reset clears flags and forces every channel to a terminal mode marker, asserts gate except for channel two, reloads zero count, and resets reinject accounting.
Extended state restore detects a rising transition into legacy mode and requests start behavior only for the channel zero reload.

Range comparison orders by start address and, for nonzero probe length, by end address, treating zero length probe as exact address match and leaving overlapping order to a caller that scans all matches.
Registration rejects when the non eventfd device count reaches the table limit, fails cleanly on allocation failure, otherwise inserts at the first greater position preserving sorted order.
Pin level represents logical OR across source identifiers maintained as bits in a shared state word, setting the caller bit on asserted level and clearing it otherwise.
Level sensitive pins set or clear both request and history together with level, while edge sensitive pins set request only on rising history transition and always track history.
Masked pin injection returns a distinct negative marker, otherwise it reports whether the request bit changed state.
Priority scan starts from a configurable offset and returns the first set bit position, with an empty mask returning a sentinel beyond the valid range.

Pending selection masks requests by inverted mask, suppresses the slave cascade bit from service comparison under special fully nested master mode, and signals only when pending priority outranks service priority.
Slave pending request is propagated as pulsed cascade pin activity on the master before master selection drives the output request line.

Acknowledge sets service state, clears request only for edge sensitive pins, optionally handles automatic end of interrupt with rotation, and synthesizes fallback vectors for missing slave or master requests.
Acknowledge clears the global output marker before selection so that a fresh level can be recomputed after state update.

Reset preserves level sensitive requests, clears edge history and mask and priority offset and special mask and read selector, forces init state, conditionally clears nested and automatic modes, and clears service only when some vCPU can accept PIC interrupt.
Chip selector maps pin numbers below eight to the master identifier and all others to the slave identifier.
Mask broadcast resolves chip plus pin to a global number and invokes only notifiers registered for that number under a source read guard.
PIC logging helpers prefix messages with the module name and rate limit unimplemented feature reports.
Interval timer header defines an include guard marker.
All PIT channel and flag accesses in port and ioctl paths hold the PIT mutex, with teardown holding the slots lock only around bus unregistration.
Bus registration requires the caller to hold the slots lock and publishes the replacement table with ordered assignment while freeing the old table after a grace period.

PIC state is guarded by a spinlock with paired helpers, with the service clear path temporarily releasing and reacquiring around external callbacks and deferred wakeup processed after unlock by kicking the first capable vCPU.
Mask notifier list traversal holds the interrupt source read lock across mapping and iteration.

Channel state carries full count including the overflow value, plus latched count, latch presence markers, status byte, read and write sequencing markers, write latch, transfer mode, operating mode, BCD marker, gate marker, and load timestamp.

PIT state carries three channels with flags, periodic marker, period in nanoseconds, timer, then mutex, reinject and pending and acknowledge counters, and acknowledge notifier, with fields before the mutex covered by that mutex.
PIT object carries timer device, speaker device, back pointer to the VM, embedded state, mask notifier, worker handle, and expired work item.
Write sequencer cycles through first word part to second word part and back for word mode, while single byte modes stay fixed and load immediately.
Read sequencer stays fixed for single byte modes and toggles between word parts for word mode, while latched word consumption moves from low expectation to high expectation then to unlatch.

Data port writes walk init states from base programming through an optional intermediate stage to mode programming then to normal mask updates, with command port writes distinguishing init command and operation control and end of interrupt families.

End of interrupt handling clears the highest service priority and optionally advances the priority offset, with dedicated commands for specific clear, offset set, and combined offset plus clear, each followed by output refresh except plain rotation toggles.
Operation control writes select poll mode, read register selection, and special mask state without changing interrupt priority.
Mask updates record changed bits and emit per pin mask notifications with the new masked state before refreshing output.
Output latch records wakeup need only on rising transition from clear to asserted.
Timer and speaker device operations dispatch port reads and writes to channel and speaker handlers.
Mask change entry resets reinject accounting when the line becomes unmasked.
State ioctls copy channel arrays and flags between userspace structures and kernel state under lock, with extended get clearing its reserved area.
PIC port writes decode the low address bit to select command versus data behavior.
Service clear drops the PIC spinlock while notifying external listeners, so concurrent interrupt arrivals can interleave after state update and must be tolerated.
Port read copy truncates length to the local result size to avoid overrun of the fixed width destination.
Pin injection validates the pin range and returns a negative sentinel on out of range input.
Timer port base address is decimal sixty four.
Speaker port address is decimal ninety seven.
Timer port block length is four bytes.
Nominal PIT input frequency is one million one hundred ninety three thousand one hundred eighty one ticks per second.
Channel selection mask keeps the low two address bits.
Maximum PIT interrupt interval equals the system tick rate divided by one hundred.
